Comment marche ce screener

What a 57% win rate actually buys you

6 août 20266.5/10

Buying a leader at its high is the most common way to lose money in a trend that is working. You pay the worst available price for the comfort of late confirmation, and the first ordinary retreat shakes you out of a position that was right about the company and wrong about the entry. The pullback signal exists to answer one question. When do you step into an advance that is still intact without paying the top of it? Every filter in it serves that question, and it measures nothing else.

It starts by refusing anything that is not already trending. Price above its two hundred day line, a series of higher lows, the plain stage two structure that any chart reader recognizes. Only then does it hunt for the retreat, graded against the Fibonacci retracement bands, volume drying up on the down days, the entry sitting close to a visible support level. Those filters all point at one number that never shows on the board, the distance between your entry and your stop. Shallow retreat plus close support equals a tight stop. That is the entire economic thesis of the screener, and the mechanism behind it is ordinary. Profit taking inside an established advance drags price back toward the moving average, where the buyers who missed the first leg come back in. Holders who still believe do not sell into weakness, so volume fades as the price slips, and support catches it before the trend itself breaks.

Now the number, and I am going to give it to you straight because nobody else will. The pullback signal clears my doctrine gate as VALID rather than MARGINAL. Its five day win rate is **57%** across **2158** signals. That sits above a coin flip by a margin you should respect and never oversell. If someone hands you a hit rate in the high fifties and calls it an edge, they are selling you something. The edge lives in the asymmetry the setup buys you, a stop you can hold in your hand against a target above the top of the base. **57%** is enough because the loser is small by construction. It stops being enough the moment you widen the stop.

You can look at it yourself. Open the Pullback tab, sort by distance to support, and read the CONVICTION column before you read anything else. **751** signals fired on yesterday's board, so the list is fresh. Click a name for the Deep Dive and check what kills it. Support breaking on heavy volume, or the two hundred day line losing its slope. At that point the trend has changed, and the screener has nothing useful left to say. The board is live at /screeners?view=dip.

À surveiller La distance au support la plus courte avec un volume qui s'éteint sur les down days ; le setup meurt si le support casse sur volume lourd ou si la 200 jours perd sa pente.
